repo/README.md:103:- **Administrators only (since 2026-10-24, perm-run01)**: the permission console and the whole data channel are for system administrators only. A system administrator is a row of the `users` table of this system with `isAdmin: 'y'` **and** `isActive: 'y'` (this package takes its own table as the authority, never the `isAdmin` your `getUserByToken` reports). After the full check described below, the connection gate, the executing identity and the console login check (`/api/getUserByToken`) additionally require that row to be an administrator; otherwise they refuse with the fixed message key `userNotAdmin` (the connection gate answers `permission denied`, srLog `verifyConn-error` with `msg: 'userNotAdmin'`), **even when your `verifyClientUser` lets the user in**. An ordinary user (`isAdmin: 'n'`) therefore cannot reach the data channel (no `select` on the four tables, no read-only function, no system function, no upload or download entry) and cannot log in to the console; the only thing an ordinary user can do is ask for his or her own permission tree with a token through `/api/getPerm` (application systems keep using `/api/getPermUserInfor` and `/syncAndReplaceTabs` with their application token). The console shows "No permission to enter the permission console" and stays on that notice instead of redirecting. Your `verifyClientUser` still runs first and can only tighten further; it no longer needs to tell administrators from ordinary users by `from`, and it must **not** return `user.isAdmin === 'y'` (that would also refuse ordinary users on `/api/getPerm`). Entry inventory:
repo/README.md:113:  | `GET /api/getPermUserInfor`, `POST /syncAndReplaceTabs` | application systems (`verifyAppUser`) | handlers → `getAndVerifyAppUser` |
repo/README.md:118:- **Function-level role check (behavior change)**: `updateTargets`, `updatePemis`, `updateGrups` and `updateUsers` now refuse a caller whose row in the `users` table is not active **and** does not have `isAdmin: 'y'`, with the fixed message key `userNotAdmin`, before anything is read or written (srLog `requireAdmin-error`: function name and user id only). The `users` table of this system is the authority; the `isAdmin` that your `getUserByToken` reports is not used for this check (as for `isAdmin` elsewhere). Until now these functions relied entirely on your `verifyClientUser`; if it let non-administrators in (a read-only viewer, for example), they could write. The bundled pages are administrator pages and are unaffected. Count `requireAdmin-error` in srLog to see whether anyone was relying on the old behavior. *(Since perm-run01 an ordinary user is already refused at the connection gate, before this check; `requireAdmin` remains as defense in depth and is only reachable if the caller's role is lowered between the gate and the function. The read-only functions are restricted as well, see "Administrators only" above.)*
repo/README.md:119:- **Public entries**: there are none apart from the static front-end files. `/api/getUserByToken` verifies a client user and requires an administrator, `/api/getPerm` verifies a client user (any role), `/api/getPermUserInfor` and `/syncAndReplaceTabs` verify an application user (`verifyAppUser`); the data channel only offers `select` on the tables (all writes go through the four functions above).
repo/README.md:126:- **What changes**: a user whose row in the `users` table of this system is not an active administrator (`isAdmin` not `'y'`, or `isActive` not `'y'`) is now refused by the connection gate (all data-channel entries, including `select` on the four tables, `getWebInfor`, `getStaEvent`, `getStaEventTable`, system functions and the upload and download routes), by the executing identity check of the request body token, and by the console login check `GET /api/getUserByToken`, **even when your `verifyClientUser` lets that user in**. The refusal key is `userNotAdmin` (the connection gate answers `permission denied`; srLog `verifyConn-error` with `msg: 'userNotAdmin'`, `getUserIdByToken-error`, `getAndVerifyAdminUser-error` and `api/getUserByToken-error`: the caller's `from` only, never the token). Before this release the read access was only as strict as your `verifyClientUser`: an ordinary user your function let in could read all four tables; since 2026-10-23 (perm-run03) only the four write functions checked the role.
repo/README.md:127:- **What stays the same**: `/api/getPerm` stays open to every valid user your `verifyClientUser` lets in and returns the caller's own permission tree only; `/api/getPermUserInfor` and `/syncAndReplaceTabs` (application systems, `verifyAppUser`) are unchanged; your `verifyClientUser` is still called first and can still tighten; `isAdmin` is read from the `users` table of this system, never from your `getUserByToken`.
repo/README.md:128:- **What you can drop**: your `verifyClientUser` no longer has to tell administrators from ordinary users by `from` (it may still tighten). Do **not** make it return `user.isAdmin === 'y'` unless you want to refuse ordinary users on `/api/getPerm` as well (the old example did exactly that; the JSDoc and the example above now show `return true`). Ordinary users cannot use the console: it shows "No permission to enter the permission console" (eng / cht) and stays on it, without redirecting to `urlRedirect`.
repo/README.md:129:- **Check before upgrading**: list the rows of `users` with `isAdmin: 'n'` that currently use the console through your `verifyClientUser`; they will be refused after the upgrade. Count `verifyConn-error` with `msg: 'userNotAdmin'` in srLog afterwards to see who is still trying. The message key `userNotAdmin` now reads "Only system administrators can access or change this data" (it was "...can change this data").
repo/README.md:153:**3. Caller identity** — see "Security: caller identity" above (the body token is verified like the header token; the four write functions need `isAdmin: 'y'` in the `users` table: `userNotAdmin`).
repo/README.md:155:**4. Login mapping `mappingBy: 'id'` (the default) follows `srcKey` for externally synchronized users, login values must be unique across all rows and sources, and `getPermUserInfor` follows the same mapping (behavior change, perm-run04; tightened in perm-run05)**
repo/README.md:156:- **The rule**: the id that your `getUserByToken` returns is matched, among the rows of the `users` table, against the `id` of a row created in the admin pages (`from` empty, as before) and against the **`srcKey`** of a row synchronized from an external source (`from` not empty); a login needs exactly one matching row and that row must be active (perm-run05: matches are counted whether or not the rows are active, see "A clash is refused at every entrance" below). The `id` of an external row is the internal primary key that this system generates (section 1); it is **no longer a login identity**, so a user imported after the upgrade logs in with the id of the source system (the `srcKey` you sent), and everything inside the system (the pages, `userId` / `userIdUpdate`, `getUserIdByToken`) uses the internal `id` of the row. `mappingBy: 'email'` and `'name'` are unchanged (they never looked at `srcKey`). Two things follow for your deployment: (a) the id returned by `getUserByToken` must identify one person across **all** your sources, and (perm-run05) it must be unique across all sources **whether or not the rows are active** (the login does not know which source a token came from, and different external systems often hand out the same user id to different people, so a disabled user of one source must never let a token reach the active user of another source with the same value; the import and the admin pages now refuse to store such a pair, and a login that matches more than one row is refused with `ambiguousUserFromPerm`); (b) **`/api/getPermUserInfor?userId=` and `getPermUserInfor(url, token, userId)` resolve `userId` by the same login mapping (behavior change, perm-run05)**: with `mappingBy: 'id'` pass the id of the source system, that is the **`srcKey`** of an external row or the `id` of an admin row, not the internal `id` that this system generated; a value that matches more than one row is refused (HTTP answer `ambiguousUserFromPerm`, the SDK rejects with `cannotGetUserDataByUrl`), and a value that matches no active row answers the all-`n` rules of an unknown user, as before. A caller that passes the internal `id` of an external row now gets those empty rules (the user is not found), unless that value happens to equal the login value of another row, in which case it gets that other row's rules (the same rule as a login), so update such callers to pass the `srcKey`. With `mappingBy: 'email'` or `'name'` `userId` is still the internal `id` of the row, as before. `/api/getPerm` (the signed-in user's own permissions) is not affected.
repo/README.md:189:- **External rows are protected from the admin pages (behavior change, `opt.lockExternalRows`, default `'y'`)**: a row whose `from` is a non-empty string is an *external row* (normally written by an application through `/syncAndReplaceTabs`, which only accepts a non-empty `from`); a row whose `from` is `''`, missing, or not a string (`null`, number, boolean) is an *admin row*. With `lockExternalRows: 'y'` the server enforces the following for the admin pages and for direct `updateTargets` / `updatePemis` / `updateGrups` / `updateUsers` calls alike. The whole save is refused, nothing is written and nothing is silently ignored: (1) a **new** row must have `from === ''` (a copy of an external row, a re-created row and a typed value are all refused), and an admin row cannot be turned into a row with a non-empty `from`: `saveFromNotAllowed`; (2) an external row cannot be **deleted**, cannot change its `from`, and cannot change any identity / structure field (every schema field except `id`, `from`, `order`, the assignment field and the server-managed fields `userId` / `timeCreate` / `userIdUpdate` / `timeUpdate`; for `users` this includes `name`, `email`, `isAdmin` and `isActive`): `saveExternalRowChanged`. The **assignment fields** (`users.cgrups`, `grups.cpemis`, `pemis.crules`; targets have none) stay writable from the admin pages ("Lv1"), but changing one on an external row needs the load baseline described below. The `order` of an external row belongs to the external source (a save does not renumber it), and an external row that differs from the stored one only in server-managed fields counts as unchanged. `opt.lockExternalRows: 'n'` restores the old behavior (only the `from` type check of the next item remains). The setting is returned by `getWebInfor()` as `lockExternalRows` (`'y'` / `'n'`).
repo/README.md:190:- **The admin pages show external rows as read-only**: a lock icon with a tooltip in the first column, a banner above the list (rendered only when the table has external rows or there is a synchronization warning; otherwise the page is exactly as before), the `from` column read-only on every row (also with `lockExternalRows: 'n'`; before this release it could be edited in the list pages), the `isAdmin` / `isActive` check boxes of an external user disabled, "delete" skipping external rows with a notice, and "copy" resetting `from` to `''`. This is a convenience: the server is the enforcer (a paste into a read-only cell, see the known limitations below, is stopped by the page before sending and by the server anyway).
repo/README.md:191:- **An administrator cannot disable or delete an external user (policy)**: identity fields, including `isActive` and `isAdmin`, belong to the external source. To disable an external user urgently, do it at the source (push the source's rows without that user, or with `isActive: 'n'`, and wait for the next synchronization) or remove the source's rows offline with `g_purgeFrom.mjs` (see the upgrade steps below). There is no local "disable override" on purpose (the next synchronization would overwrite it), and no way to "claim" an external row as an admin row (the source would then be refused for that id, `idOtherFrom`).
repo/README.md:205:- **Objects are iterated by their own keys**: a field or key named `length` is an ordinary key everywhere user-supplied objects are walked (write validation, the `cgrups` / `cpemis` / `crules` JSON strings evaluated by `getPerm` / `getPermUserInfor`, and the list pages). Before, lodash treated such an object as an array-like of that length: real keys were skipped (for example a group listed next to `"length": 0` was ignored, so its rules evaluated to `n`) and a huge `length` made the call spin or run out of memory.
repo/README.md:207:- **Authorization lookups use the exact id, not a lodash path (behavior change, tightening)**: `getUserRules` (used by `getPerm` / `getPermUserInfor`), the SDK `perm().active(name)` and the edit dialogs of user groups, group permissions and permission rules now look a target, group or permission up by its exact name as an own property. Before, a name containing `.` or `[` was resolved as a path: when only `A` was granted, targets `A.0` and `A[0]` evaluated to `y` (and `A.length` to `1`), and inherited names such as `toString` could be returned. Names that are themselves keys (for example a target called `A.0` granted by a rule named `A.0`, or one called `constructor` / `__proto__`) are granted as usual. In the admin session of `modeEditUsers: 'for:grups'`, a database id containing `.` or `[` can no longer be taken over by another row's nested field. The edit dialogs also keep an item named `__proto__` when saving (before, it was shown as enabled but silently dropped from the saved JSON).
repo/README.md:211:- **Edit dialogs decode authorization data exactly like the server (behavior change, tightening)**: `cgrups` / `cpemis` / `crules` may also be written in the array form `[{ "name": "A", "isActive": "y" }]` (an external application writing directly; `getPerm` / `getPermUserInfor` already honor it). The edit dialogs for user groups, group permissions and permission rules (and the two "belongs to" dialogs) used to look entries up by name, showed such entries as disabled, and saving revoked the authorization. They now decode both forms with the same function as the server, so what a dialog shows matches what is authorized, and saving keeps the authorization unchanged. Details: (1) in `cgrups` / `cpemis`, an entry with `isActive: "y"` but a missing or invalid `mode` (anything other than `"OR"` / `"AND"`) is not honored by the server; the dialogs now show it as disabled (before, object-form entries like that were shown as enabled and saving filled in `OR`, silently granting it) **[superseded on 2026-10-21 by the "Conflicting or ambiguous authorization data" item below: such an entry is now honored by the server as a restriction (it only intersects with the other entries and never grants on its own), and the dialogs show it as an enabled `AND` entry]**; (2) in the object form `{ "<name>": { "name": …, … } }` the outer key is the name and an inner `name` is ignored, also in the "belongs to" dialogs (before, saving there re-pointed the grant to the inner name); (3) the three direct editors always save the object form `{ "<name>": … }`, the two "belongs to" dialogs rewrite the stored string only when its decoded content changes; (4) see the next two items for the new merge rule (order independent) and for the case the object form cannot hold (the same name active as both `AND` and `OR`).
repo/README.md:215:- **`/syncAndReplaceTabs` requires non-empty string names and ids (behavior change)**: for `grups` and `pemis` the `name` of every row, and for `targets` the `id` of every row, must be a non-empty string (as the admin pages already required). A missing value, an empty string, or a non-string (number, boolean, `null`) rejects the whole push with `invalidRows` before anything is deleted. Before, a group or permission with `name: ""` was stored and honored by `getPerm` / `getPermUserInfor`, but the edit dialogs treated it as invalid and removed it on the next save. `users` rows are not affected.
repo/README.md:217:- **A rule name that cannot be a property key no longer fails the whole query (bug fix, 2026-10-21)**: `crules` is valid JSON even when an element of the array form has a `name` such as `{"toString": null}`, which JavaScript cannot turn into a key. Before, `getPerm` / `getPermUserInfor` threw for every user holding that permission and returned the engine message (`Cannot convert object to primitive value`) to the calling application. Now that element is ignored (it matches no target) and the rest of the rules are evaluated as usual; the same holds for the permission-rule edit dialog and the list pages. Any other failure while evaluating a user's rules is logged and answered with the fixed key `cannotGetUserRules`, never with the engine message.
repo/README.md:218:- **Group and permission names must be unique (behavior change, 2026-10-21, F-02)**: authorization looks groups and permissions up by name (the server takes the first row with that name), so two rows with the same name made the result depend on the database row order. The admin pages already rejected duplicates; `/syncAndReplaceTabs` now rejects a push for `grups` or `pemis` with `invalidRows` (before anything is deleted, nothing changes) when two rows of the push share a `name`, or when a `name` is already used by a row of another `from` (rows of the same `from` are replaced by the push and do not count). Names are compared exactly: `Admin`, `admin` and `Admin ` are different names. +# 二、對標與對稱
+
+[Django AdminSite.has_permission](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/ref/contrib/admin/#django.contrib.admin.AdminSite.has_permission) 預設要求啟用且具後台資格；[OWASP 授權指引](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html) 要求每次請求在伺服端驗權，並依已認證身分限制可取資料。本套件分開後台、資料 API 及本人權限入口，方向相符。下表是依本套件程式作的比較，不表示上述系統保證所有提交時競態均已解決。
+
+| 元素 | 實際處理 | 對稱性判斷 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| checkToken | getAndVerifyAdminUser(token,from)，`WWebPerm.mjs:589–594` | 所有 apiType 原樣傳 from，沒有略過管理員檢查的分支 |
+| getUserIdByToken | getAndVerifyAdminUser(token,'main')，`1186`；回 perm 內 id | main 與連線閘對稱；兩 token 可為不同人是刻意契約 |
+| /api/getUserByToken | getAndVerifyAdminUser(token,'getUserByToken')，`833` | 登入即拒非管理員，資料 API 仍另驗 |
+| /api/getPerm | getAndVerifyClientUser(token,'getPerm')，`883` | 刻意允許一般使用者，但未保持解析出的列是 #3 缺陷 |
+| /api/getPermUserInfor | getAndVerifyAppUser(tokenSelf,'getPermUserInfor')，`959`；目標另解析 | 刻意的服務授權，可查別人；呼叫者不須有 perm 列 |
+| /syncAndReplaceTabs | getAndVerifyAppUser(token,'syncAndReplaceTabs')，`1058`；驗表名及 payload | 刻意的服務寫入入口，不在 perm 管理員判準內 |

+| /api/getPermUserInfor | getAndVerifyAppUser(tokenSelf,'getPermUserInfor')，`959`；目標另解析 | 刻意的服務授權，可查別人；呼叫者不須有 perm 列 |

+五條資料通道的對應為 POST /api/ulctr → upload-controller、POST /api/slc → upload-slice、POST /api/dwgfn → download-get-filename、GET /api/dwgf → download-get-file、POST /api/dw → download（`server/WWebPerm.mjs:58`、`586`；`test/api-adminOnly.test.mjs:202–207`）。verifyConn 在 `1143` 將 apiType 原樣交給 checkToken，`592` 再原樣交給管理員 helper；main 的標頭與本體兩次部署驗證都用 main，登入用 getUserByToken、本人查詢用 getPerm。app 驗證則分別用 getPermUserInfor、syncAndReplaceTabs。未見 from 拼字或通道分流導致的角色閘遺漏。
